name: Gut Geography — Neural-Feed Visceral Art Series
creator: Collective: Miriam Oduya-Henriksen, Priya Subramaniam-Volkov, and Tunde Adesanya-Cho
description: A series of neural-feed art works that bypass visual and auditory cortex entirely, transmitting directly to interoceptive and proprioceptive processing centers — viewers experience the work as sensations in their own bodies rather than as perceived imagery. Works in the series include 'Hunger Atlas' (the mapped geography of a the Gray Zone resident's chronic malnutrition rendered as the viewer's own felt absence), 'The Weight of Debt' (a precise somatic simulation of a Tier 2 worker's cortisol levels across a twelve-hour shift), and 'Bloom After Damage' (a post-surgical augmentation recovery rendered as felt experience). Each work runs approximately four minutes.
cultural_impact: Widely credited with creating a new category of art criticism around somatic fidelity and the ethics of induced suffering-as-empathy; the series generated more Tier 3-4 charitable giving to the Gray Zone health organizations than any campaign in the prior decade.
controversy: Several viewers reported lasting phantom sensations following 'Hunger Atlas'; a class action suit alleging undisclosed neurological side effects was settled privately. The series was pulled from licensed neural feeds and continues to circulate on pirate channels.
story_hooks: A Tier 4 executive who experienced 'Hunger Atlas' on a dare cannot stop feeling the phantom hunger; six weeks later, she is funding the Gray Zone food infrastructure and cannot explain why to her board.
One of the three artists wants to end the series; the other two believe they are legally and ethically obligated to keep distributing it for free, and the collective is fracturing.
Someone has created an unauthorized fourth work in the series titled 'Overdose' — and people who experience it are ending up catatonic.
